summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,200-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views. The best videos are short 'this device doesn't see/hear the way you think' surprises about relatable gadgets like robots, clap switches and motion sensors, which get the most likes, saves and shares. Generic 'How does X work?' questions about everyday places (lift, mall door, tap, street light, smoke detector) get much less attention, and the English video got no Instagram reach at all.
winningPattern: Hindi Instagram Reels about a hands-on maker gadget (robot, clap switch, PIR/IR sensor, mic) with a myth-busting, counterintuitive hook such as 'X doesn't do what you think, it only does Y'. Titles are short, punchy statements in Hinglish with one emoji, often naming a robot or a familiar action (clap, whistle). The best ones lean on a surprising 'without/doesn't/only' contrast and relatable robot visuals, and they get the most saves and shares.
doMore: Lead with a surprising contradiction in the first line: 'X can't see/hear, it only feels Y'
Pick maker-favourite subjects: robots, clap switch, PIR/IR sensors, mics, gyro, since these consistently hit 1,200+ IG views
Make follow-ups to winners, e.g. clap switch part 3 or robot-without-sensor series, and link them to each other
Add a save or share trigger at the end, like 'save this for your next project' or 'send to your Arduino friend'
Post YouTube versions separately and test different titles and thumbnails, since YT views are almost flat compared with IG
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' titles on public-place devices (lift, mall door, washroom tap, smoke detector), which got 60-570 IG views
Publishing English-only Shorts to Instagram-less audiences, or posting without cross-posting to IG, since the English video got zero IG reach
Near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector, two IR sensor, two automatic tap videos) that split the audience
